detail.readme:
# mirroir-mcp [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/mirroir-mcp)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mirroir-mcp) [![Build](https://github.com/jfarcand/mirroir-mcp/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jfarcand/mirroir-mcp/actions/workflows/build.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue)](LICENSE) [![macOS 15+](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS-15%2B-black?logo=apple)](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1481795325953048627?logo=discord&label=Discord)](https://discord.gg/u8ug9QCSqF) ### Let your agent use your real iPhone: errands across your apps, automations, even games.

Website · Demos · Set up with your agent · Tools · Changelog · Discord

A saved recipe reel becomes a grocery list in Reminders. The agent listens to the video and reads its frames. A real iPhone, sped up.

No Developer Mode, no Xcode, no WebDriverAgent, no jailbreak. mirroir-mcp works through macOS iPhone Mirroring, so it reaches any app on your phone, including App Store apps you could never build. It works from any MCP client, with [42 tools](docs/tools.md). It uses the apps already signed in on your phone: no connector, no OAuth, no password handed to anyone. ## What people build - **A saved recipe reel becomes a grocery list.** The agent opens the reel, reads its frames with `describe_screen`, hears the narration with [`listen`](docs/tools.md#listening), then types the ingredients into Reminders. That is the run in the GIF above. - **Errands across apps.** Read the commute time in Waze, then post it in Slack: the agent carries what one app shows into another. [Watch the demo](https://mirroir.dev/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=body#demo). The same errand as a skill (Waze to Messages) is in [Skills, exploration and CI](docs/skills-and-ci.md#skills). - **Games.** A [`scene:` step](docs/skills-marketplace.md#scenes) plays a turn-based or tap-driven game, frame by frame, under a hard frame, token and time budget; a run that runs out of budget is inconclusive (exit 66), never a silent pass. [`touch`](docs/tools.md#games-and-multi-touch) holds a finger for virtual joysticks, `hold_keys` drives games that take keyboard and mouse, and `pinch` and `rotate` zoom and rotate. iPhone Mirroring exposes a single pointer, so twin-stick games stay out of reach. See [Games](docs/games.md).

A real game on a real iPhone: the model reads the board, Stockfish picks the moves, mirroir plays them against Chess.com's strongest bot. The opening runs at 2.5×, the middle game at 45×, the finish at 2×.

## Quick start You need macOS 15 or later and an iPhone connected through [iPhone Mirroring](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421). Paste this into your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, …): ```text Set up mirroir-mcp so you can drive my iPhone: follow https://github.com/jfarcand/mirroir-mcp/blob/main/docs/onboarding.md step by step, and finish by reading back what my iPhone screen shows. ``` Or install it yourself: ```bash npx -y mirroir-mcp install # or: brew tap jfarcand/tap && brew install mirroir-mcp npx -y mirroir-mcp doctor # names anything left to fix ``` OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code and the other clients: [Install](docs/install.md). Then ask for something: ``` Open Calendar, create a new event called "Dentist" next Tuesday at 2pm. ``` ``` Open my Expo Go app, tap "LoginDemo", test the login screen with test@example.com / password123. Screenshot after each step. ``` ``` Start recording, open Instagram, scroll the feed and open my profile, stop recording. ``` ## Build your own agent - **Any MCP client.** Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop and the others connect to the same [42 tools](docs/tools.md). It also installs as a Claude Code plugin, an OpenClaw skill from ClawHub, or a Hermes Agent plugin that asks before every call that can change the phone: see [Install](docs/install.md). - **Proven steps in one call.** Once a sequence has worked, [`run_steps`](docs/tools.md#tool-list) replays it in one call (`"tap: "`, `"type: calculator"`, `"wait_for: Get"`). Every step is checked against the permission policy before the first runs, and the run stops at the first failure. - **Skills.** Capture a workflow you repeat as a [SKILL.md](docs/skills-and-ci.md#skills): numbered steps the AI follows, matched on screen text, not coordinates. `generate_skill` explores an app and writes them for you. Ready-made skills live in [mirroir-skills](https://github.com/jfarcand/mirroir-skills); the format is in [Skills Marketplace](docs/skills-marketplace.md). - **Agents keep notes.** `save_note` keeps one line per lesson per app, and `get_notes` gives it to the next session. - **An agent on another machine.** [`mirroir-mcp serve`](docs/cli.md#serve) speaks MCP over HTTP on 127.0.0.1 only, behind a bearer token; reach it through an SSH port forward. `install-agent` keeps it running as a LaunchAgent from its own signed "mirroir serve" bundle, so its grants survive upgrades. ## Why mirroir - **Nothing to install on the phone.** The iPhone stays stock: no signing, no provisioning profile, no on-device agent. If iPhone Mirroring shows it, mirroir can drive it. - **Your Mac stays yours.** Taps, typing and swipes reach the mirror without bringing it to the front, so you can keep working. Drags and two-finger gestures bring it forward for a moment, then hand your app back. - **It hears the phone, too.** [`listen`](docs/tools.md#listening) turns what the phone plays, a reel's narration or a voice message, into text. It records only iPhone Mirroring's sound, and macOS transcribes it on the Mac: the audio never leaves it. Needs macOS 26; since 0.47.0. ## Testing and CI The run an agent makes once can become a test that runs without it. - **Explore once, replay without an LLM.** `generate_skill` explores an app and writes [SKILL.md](docs/skills-and-ci.md#skills) files. A compiled skill replays from the CLI with no AI in the loop (`mirroir test`), so CI runs are deterministic and cost no tokens. - **One test across phone, web and backend.** [`mirroir-run`](docs/mirroir-run.md) is our companion test runner, a separate binary. One YAML scenario can drive the iPhone, a browser, HTTP endpoints and subprocesses, then compare what the page and the phone showed. See [Web and iOS in one scenario](docs/web-and-ios.md). - **Drift fails loudly.** `mirroir-run` has a third verdict beside pass and fail: `DRIFT`, exit code **65**, when every assertion held but the output moved past its baseline. Your CI lane decides whether drift blocks a merge. ### How it compares | | mirroir | [phone-harness](https://github.com/phone-harness/phone-harness) | [mobile-mcp](https://github.com/mobile-next/mobile-mcp) | [Appium](https://github.com/appium/appium) | |---|---|---|---|---| | Physical iPhone, no Developer Mode or signing | Yes — stock phone via iPhone Mirroring | Yes — stock phone via iPhone Mirroring | USB-connected, trusted device (see its README) | No — WebDriverAgent via Xcode, Developer Mode | | App Store apps you can't build | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes, on a provisioned device | | Your own iPhone from any MCP client | Yes | No — its MCP server is cloud-only; local phones use its CLI | Yes | Through the separate [appium-mcp](https://github.com/appium/appium-mcp) | | Replay without an LLM | Yes — compiled skills, `mirroir test` | Python scripts you write; no recorder or compiled replay | No — the agent drives every run | Yes — test code | | Distinct drift verdict | Yes — `DRIFT`, exit 65 | No | No | No — pass / fail | | One scenario across iPhone + web + HTTP | Yes — `mirroir-run` | No | No | Via your own test code | | Android | No — an emulator window can be driven only as a generic macOS window | Yes | Yes | Yes | | iOS Simulator | No | No | Yes | Yes | | Hosted cloud phones | No | Yes — Phone Harness Cloud | Yes — Mobile Next Cloud | Via third-party device clouds | phone-harness is the closest tool here: it also drives a stock iPhone through iPhone Mirroring, and it adds Android and hosted phones, which mirroir doesn't have. mobile-mcp and Appium cover Android and simulators too. mirroir goes further after the agent's first run: that run becomes a replay that needs no LLM, and a test that tells you when the output moves. ## Safety Giving an AI access to your phone demands defense in depth, so mirroir-mcp is **fail-closed**. - **Read-only until you say otherwise.** Without a config file, only the 14 read-only tools are exposed. Every tool that changes something stays hidden from the client until you allow it in [`permissions.json`](docs/permissions.md). - **Sensitive apps can be blocked.** `blockedApps` keeps the AI out of apps like Wallet or Banking, even when other tools are allowed. - **Passwords stay yours.** mirroir never presses a sheet that asks for a password or Touch ID, and it tells agents to ask you before sending, buying, deleting or changing a setting. - **No root, no telemetry, no daemon unless you install one.** It runs as your user with Screen Recording and Accessibility, and lives and dies with your MCP client; only the opt-in [`serve` agent](docs/security.md) keeps running, on loopback, behind a token. The one network call it makes by default is a once-a-day version check against npm (`updateCheck: false` turns it off). What your agent reads from the screen goes to whichever model your client uses. - **Kill switch.** Quit iPhone Mirroring, unlock the iPhone, lock the Mac's screen, or quit your MCP client: each stops all input at once, and nothing reopens the app for the agent. See [Security](docs/security.md) for the full threat model. ## Documentation | | | |---|---| | [Install](docs/install.md) | Every install path, per-client setup, updating, uninstalling | | [Onboarding](docs/onboarding.md) | Setup written for the agent: prerequisites, install, doctor, a read-only proof, and an optional first errand | | [Tools Reference](docs/tools.md) | All 42 tools, parameters, and input workflows | | [How mirroir sees the screen](docs/screen-intelligence.md) | The observe, reason, act loop; OCR, icon detection, AI vision | | [Skills, exploration and CI](docs/skills-and-ci.md) | APP.md, skills, `generate_skill`, `mirroir test`, compiled replay, AI diagnosis, patterns | | [`mirroir-run`](docs/mirroir-run.md) | Replay across iPhone, web, HTTP and subprocesses; GitHub Actions; Maestro import | | [Games](docs/games.md) | Shell and scene, the `scene:` step, game controls | | [CLI Tools](docs/cli.md) | Recorder, doctor, keyboard layout, `serve` over HTTP | | [Configuration](docs/configuration.md) | All settings: screen intelligence, input timing, exploration, AI providers | | [FAQ](docs/faq.md) | Security, focus stealing, keyboard layouts, embacle/vision mode | | [Security](docs/security.md) | Threat model, kill switch, and recommendations | | [Privacy](docs/privacy.md) | What mirroir reads, sends and stores | | [Permissions](docs/permissions.md) | Fail-closed permission model and config file | | [Known Limitations](docs/limitations.md) | Focus stealing, keyboard layout gaps, autocorrect | | [Patterns & Skills](docs/components.md) | Element patterns, screen recipes, APP.md app descriptions, and the detection pipeline | | [Exploring a New App](docs/exploring-a-new-app.md) | Step-by-step playbook for onboarding a new app — APP.md, permissions, components, exploration goal | | [YOLO Icon Detection](docs/yolo-models.md) | Recommended YOLO models, CoreML setup, and configuration | | [Compiled Skills](docs/compiled-skills.md) | Zero-OCR skill replay | | [Testing](docs/testing.md) | FakeMirroring, integration tests, and CI strategy | | [Web and iOS in one scenario](docs/web-and-ios.md) | How `mirroir-run` hands iOS blocks to `mirroir-mcp`, and how `cross_surface` compares a browser with a phone | | [Cross-surface replay](runner/docs/) | `mirroir-run` scenario grammar, `.mirroir/` plan, `SAMPLE.md`, judge profiles, CI | | [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) | Debug mode and common issues | | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | How to add tools, commands, and tests | | [Skills Marketplace](docs/skills-marketplace.md) | Skill format, plugin discovery, and authoring | ## Community Join the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/u8ug9QCSqF) to ask questions, share skills, and discuss ideas.
